findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
An employee was observed using bare hands to push the actuator on the paper towel dispenser directly after washing hands. Discussed with PIC to push the paper towel actuator before washing hands or to use a barrier when getting paper towel in order to prevent recontaminating freshly washed hands. Ensure that employees are using a barrier to operate faucet handles and the actuator on the paper towel dispenser after washing hands.  

2-301.12: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles. (D) Automatic handwashing facility may be used if APPROVED.

findings.title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties
findings.citation_text:
2-102.11 (A), (B) & (C)(1), (4)-(16) Priority violations were observed for handwashing and sanitization. Active managerial controls were discussed and will be revisited at spot check in ~10 days.
Based on the risks inherent to the food operation, during inspections and upon request the PIC shall demonstrate to the regulatory authority knowledge of foodborne disease prevention, application of the hazard analysis and critical control points, and the requirements of the Code.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.14 PIC went between tasks without a hand wash. PIC was troubleshooting the sanitizer dispenser and working with chemical prior to putting on gloves to continue with prep. Proper handwashing between tasks and prior to glove use were discussed.
Food Employees shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in food preparation including working with exposed food, clean equipment and utensils, and unwrapped single-service and single-use articles. Hands shall also be washed prior to donning gloves and after engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-501.114 Quat solution at 3 part sink was observed at 100ppm. Solution was made within 1.5hrs prior to inspector’s arrival. Fresh solution was prepared and once again observed at 100ppm with instant change test strips (SCDPH) and litmus paper strips (facility). An air bubble and/or the temperature of the water used to prepare solutions were thought to be possible issues impacting concentration. PIC attempted troubleshooting by running the dispenser to remove the air bubble and making solutions with various temperatures of water. The concentration remained at 100ppm. Required concentration for the product used is 150-400ppm. Solution was manually mixed to provide concentration of 200-400ppm. Call for service was made, and new components are getting shipped for installation. Spot check will be conducted in ~10 days to check on function of chemical dispenser.
A quaternary ammonia compound solution shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions and be maintained at the concentration as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling. Use test strips when preparing solutions and verify proper concentration of 150-400ppm.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-501.114 Spray bottle containing chlorine based sanitizer and cleaner was observed at a concentration of 0ppm chlorine. PIC noted the solution was made ~1 month prior. Product is used to for sanitizing the slicer, and per product directions, requires a concentration of 100-150ppm. Packet of product was added to water and provided a concentration of 150ppm. PIC was advised to monitor the concentration of the sanitizer and refresh it as needed. Ensure the product is maintained at proper concentration.
Chemical sanitizer used in sanitizing solution for manual or mechanical warewashing shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions and be maintained at the concentration as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling. Use test strips to monitor the concentration of product used for sanitization of the slicer, and maintain the product at 100-150ppm chlorine as required by product directions.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
findings.citation_text: 2-102.11(C) (Pf) The facility did not have employee reporting agreements available during the inspection. These agreements are needed in order to ensure employees do not report to work while sick, which could spread illness or disease. Employees in the facility signed reporting agreements during the inspection to correct the violation.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.citation_text: 6-201.13 (A) (C) Observed coving on each side of the mop/utility sink to be lifting apart from the wall. Coving should be replaced or resealed to the wall. When cleaning methods other than water flushing are used for cleaning floors, the floor and wall junctures shall be coved and closed to no larger than 1mm (one thirty-second inch). Reference 6-201.13 (A).

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text: 2-301.12  (P)  Observed an employee wash his hands and turn the faucet off using his bare hands. Employees must use a paper towel to turn water off when washing hands to prevent recontamination of hands.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.citation_text: 5-205.11  (Pf) Observed food debris in the hand sink in the food prep area. Hand sinks should be used only for hand washing.

findings.title: Thermometers provided & accurate
findings.citation_text: 4-204.112  (C)  Observed no thermometer is not provided in the walk in cooler. The thermometer on the outside of the walk in cooler was inaccurate and reading 0 F. Thermometers must be accurate to ±3°F in the intended range of use. Reference 4-203.12.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
findings.citation_text:
3-305.11  (C) Food stored in an unapproved location. Food shall be protected by contamination by storing it: 1) in a clean, dry location; 2) where it is not exposed to splash, dust or other contamination; 3) at least 6 inches above the floor. Reference 3-305.11.

Observed bag of onions on floor near prep area in back. Onions must be hung at least 6 inches above the floor to protect against contamination.
